title: Determinant weights of an exterior power
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, put
$|k_0|=q$, fix $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and let
$\mathcal F_0$ be a nonzero lisse
Weil sheaf on $X_0$ with
semisimple geometric
representation. Choose a
composition series in the sense of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series], with simple factors
$A_1,\ldots,A_t$. Write $d_a=\dim A_a$ and let $\gamma_a$ be the
determinantal weight of $A_a$.
Let $R$ be the set of distinct values among the $\gamma_a$, and put

$$
r(\gamma):=\sum_{\gamma_a=\gamma}d_a,
$$

Thus $\dim V=\sum_{\gamma\in R}r(\gamma)$. For every
$0\le r\le\dim V$, every Jordan–Holder constituent of the exterior
power $\bigwedge^r\mathcal F_0$ (constituents and exterior powers of
Weil representations as in [def-real-weil-representation-operations])
has determinant weight

$$
\sum_{\gamma\in R}n_\gamma\gamma,
\qquad 0\le n_\gamma\le r(\gamma),
\qquad \sum_{\gamma\in R}n_\gamma=r.
$$

Conversely every admissible tuple $(n_\gamma)$ occurs as the
determinant weight of at least one
Jordan–Holder constituent. The input factors
$\gamma_a$ are counted with multiplicity as in
[def-mg-determinantal-weight-multiset]; the assertion concerns the
possible weights and their non-emptiness, not an equality of output
multiplicities for coincident sums.

proof.text: Fix $0\le r\le\dim V$. Use the operations and constituent convention of [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. Under the exact tensor equivalence [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence], subobjects, quotients and subquotients correspond in both directions, so the simple factors $A_a$ of the chosen series and the constituents $C$ of $\bigwedge^r\mathcal F_0$ are nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaves on the same $X_0$. Here simplicity, including nonzeroness, is exactly the condition in [def-mg-weil-composition-series]. Each occurrence in the chosen series is retained, as required by [def-mg-determinantal-weight-multiset].

Set $\lambda=\lambda_\iota$, where $\lambda_\iota(a)=2\log|\iota(a)|/\log q$ is the real weight character of [d-weights]. The finite-field convention gives $q>1$, so this normalization is defined. Apply [lem-rp-determinant-weights-agree] to each $A_a$ and to each constituent $C$ from step 1. Its curve and embedding hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses here. Its first clause gives finite geometric determinant for all these sheaves; its irreducible clause gives $\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(A_a)=\dw_\iota(A_a)=\gamma_a$ and $\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(C)=\dw_\iota(C)$. Thus every finite-geometric-determinant hypothesis of the conditional exterior-power proposition holds.

Apply [prop-ag-det-weight-exterior] to the original nonzero $\mathcal F_0$, its chosen composition series, this $r$, and $\lambda_\iota$. Step 2 identifies its input weights with the $\gamma_a$ of the present statement. Consequently its distinct-weight set $R$ and capacities $r(\gamma)=\sum_{\gamma_a=\gamma}d_a$ are exactly ours. The proposition gives, for every constituent $C$, an admissible tuple with $\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(C)=\sum_{\gamma\in R}n_\gamma\gamma$. Its converse supplies, for every admissible tuple, at least one constituent $C$ with that equality. It requires no semisimplicity of the original Weil representation.

In both directions from step 3 substitute the equality $\dw_\iota(C)=\dw_{\lambda_\iota}(C)$ already proved in step 2. The capacity inequalities and total $\sum_\gamma n_\gamma=r$ are unchanged. This proves the asserted possible weights and the non-emptiness for every tuple. Distinct tuples may give the same sum; the argument asserts existence for each tuple and makes no assertion about output multiplicities. Since $r$ was arbitrary in the specified interval, the conclusion holds for every such $r$.
